digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: Language model agents struggle with raw Linux shell actions, so the paper proposes a tailored agent-computer interface for software engineering.

digest_headlines.heading: The Agent-Computer Interface
digest_headlines.headline: The paper defines the agent-computer interface as the layer through which language model agents act on computers, and lists design principles for it.

digest_headlines.heading: SWE-agent: Designing an ACI for Software Engineering
digest_headlines.headline: SWE-agent provides search, a file viewer, a linter-guarded edit command and context management for software engineering tasks.

digest_headlines.heading: Experimental Setup
digest_headlines.headline: Experiments use SWE-bench, its Lite subset and HumanEvalFix, comparing SWE-agent with a retrieval-augmented baseline and a shell-only baseline.

digest_headlines.heading: Results
digest_headlines.headline: SWE-agent with GPT-4 Turbo resolves 12.47% of SWE-bench test tasks, and Lite ablations show interface choices change results.

digest_headlines.heading: Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Code benchmarks are largely self-contained, while SWE-bench uses real repository issues, and the authors claim the first language agent study of end-to-end software engineering.

digest_headlines.heading: Discussion
digest_headlines.headline: The authors conclude that interfaces tailored to language model strengths improve results, and suggest studying them may clarify how models differ from humans.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: The appendix covers component designs, sandboxed execution, reproducibility, limitations, and further analyses of trajectories and statistics.

repos.title: RF-DETR: Neural Architecture Search for Real-Time Detection Transformers
repos.paper_summary: RF-DETR is a specialist detection transformer that uses weight-sharing neural architecture search to discover accuracy-latency Pareto curves for target datasets without re-training. The model replaces the LW-DETR backbone with DINOv2 and applies a scheduler-free training procedure. During training, it samples random configurations of image resolution, patch size, windowed attention blocks, decoder layers, and query tokens. At inference, grid search selects specific sub-nets from this single trained model to match hardware constraints. On COCO, RF-DETR (nano) achieves 48.0 AP at 2.3 ms latency, outperforming D-FINE (nano) by 5.3 AP. The 2x-large variant reaches 60.1 AP on COCO, the first real-time detector to exceed 60 AP. On Roboflow100-VL, RF-DETR (2x-large) surpasses GroundingDINO (tiny) by 1.2 AP while running 20 times faster. The paper notes that latency measurements are sensitive to GPU power throttling, proposing a standardized buffering protocol for reproducible benchmarking.

repos.title: TurboQuant: Online Vector Quantization with Near-optimal Distortion Rate
repos.paper_summary:
TurboQuant is an online vector quantization method that achieves near-optimal distortion rates for both mean-squared error (MSE) and inner product estimation. The algorithm first applies a random rotation to input vectors, inducing a Beta distribution on coordinates. It then uses precomputed optimal scalar quantizers derived from a continuous k-means problem to encode each coordinate independently. For unbiased inner product estimation, the method combines an MSE-optimized quantizer with a 1-bit Quantized Johnson-Lindenstrauss (QJL) transform applied to the residual vector.

The paper proves that for any bit-width $b$, TurboQuant’s MSE distortion is bounded by $\frac{\sqrt{3}\pi}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{4^b}$, which is within a factor of approximately 2.7 of the information-theoretic lower bound. The inner product distortion is bounded by $\frac{\sqrt{3}\pi^2 \|y\|_2^2}{d} \cdot \frac{1}{4^b}$. Experiments on KV cache quantization show quality neutrality at 3.5 bits per channel and marginal degradation at 2.5 bits. In nearest neighbor search, TurboQuant outperforms existing product quantization techniques in recall while reducing indexing time to zero. Limitations include the requirement for unit-norm inputs, though non-unit norms can be handled by storing separate scaling factors.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: TurboQuant combines an MSE-optimal rotation-based quantizer with a 1-bit QJL residual stage to get unbiased, near-optimal inner product quantization.

digest_headlines.heading: Preliminaries
digest_headlines.headline: Coordinates of a uniform hypersphere point follow a Beta law that tends to a normal law, and QJL gives an unbiased single-bit estimator.

digest_headlines.heading: TurboQuant: High Performance Quantization
digest_headlines.headline: MSE distortion is bounded by a constant times 1/4^b, reaching 0.36 at 1 bit and 0.009 at 4 bits.

digest_headlines.heading: Experiments
digest_headlines.headline: TurboQuant matches full-precision performance on needle-in-a-haystack, and outperforms product quantization in recall while reducing indexing time to essentially zero.

repos.title: Chronos: Learning the Language of Time Series
repos.paper_summary:
Chronos is a pretrained probabilistic time series forecasting framework that adapts standard transformer language models to univariate forecasting. The method converts real-valued time series into discrete tokens by mean-scaling and quantizing values into 4,096 uniform bins. These token sequences are fed into T5 or GPT-2 architectures, which are trained via cross-entropy loss without architectural modifications. The authors pretrain models ranging from 20M to 710M parameters on 28 public datasets augmented with TSMixup convex combinations and KernelSynth Gaussian process synthetic data.

On a benchmark of 42 datasets, Chronos outperforms local statistical models like AutoARIMA and task-specific deep learning baselines such as PatchTST in both in-domain and zero-shot settings. On 27 unseen zero-shot datasets, the 710M parameter model achieves aggregated relative WQL scores comparable to methods specifically trained on those tasks. A limitation is that the fixed vocabulary restricts predictions to the training value range, potentially impairing performance on strongly trending series. Additionally, larger models exhibit slower inference times than lightweight local forecasters.

repos.title: ChatDev: Communicative Agents for Software Development
repos.paper_summary:
ChatDev is a multi-agent software development framework that uses LLM-driven agents to execute design, coding, and testing phases through structured dialogue. The system organizes work via a "chat chain," which breaks tasks into subtasks handled by pairs of agents acting as instructor and assistant. A "communicative dehallucination" mechanism reduces errors by having the assistant request specific details before generating code.

Evaluated on a dataset of 1,200 software requirements, ChatDev outperforms GPT-Engineer and MetaGPT. In Table 1, ChatDev achieves an executability score of 0.880 and a quality score of 0.395, compared to 0.415 and 0.152 for MetaGPT. Pairwise evaluations in Table 2 show ChatDev winning 77.1% of comparisons against GPT-Engineer when judged by GPT-4. Ablations in Table 4 indicate that removing agent roles drops executability from 0.880 to 0.580. Limitations include high computational costs due to multiple agents and a tendency to generate simple logic or static placeholders rather than complex database interactions, making it suitable primarily for prototypes.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: ChatDev uses chat among role-playing LLM agents, with language as the shared medium, across design, coding, and testing.

digest_headlines.heading: Related Work
digest_headlines.headline: Prior work covers LLM agents and deep learning applied to single waterfall phases, which the authors say remain isolated.

digest_headlines.heading: ChatDev
digest_headlines.headline: ChatDev pairs an instructor agent and an assistant agent per subtask, linked by a chat chain and dehallucination rules.

digest_headlines.heading: Evaluation
digest_headlines.headline: ChatDev scores highest on all four metrics and wins most pairwise comparisons against GPT-Engineer and MetaGPT.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: Authors conclude that language-based multi-agent communication improves software optimization and supports agent autonomy.

digest_headlines.heading: Limitations
digest_headlines.headline: Agents need detailed requirements, evaluation covers limited dimensions, and multi-agent runs need more tokens and time.

repos.title: In-Context Learning for Robots: Methods and Applications
repos.paper_summary:
This literature review organizes in-context learning (ICL) for robots, where neural parameters remain fixed during deployment. It classifies methods into four families: context-conditioned policies, geometric demonstration transfer, world-model-based control, and skill- and agent-based execution. The paper defines six learning horizons to distinguish between programmed control, learned policies, history-based adaptation, task inference from teaching, recursive self-improvement, and cross-embodiment knowledge exchange.

The analysis focuses on how contextual evidence resolves ambiguity in existing motor competence without fine-tuning weights. It examines the role of training relationships, correspondence, and memory in preserving task requirements across changes in objects, environments, and execution conditions. The review synthesizes evaluation practices to separate responsiveness to teaching, physical transfer, and benefits from retained experience. Limitations include the reliance on broad pretraining for baseline competence and the difficulty of validating transfer when physical realization changes while task relations must survive. The paper proposes a research agenda linking compositional task acquisition with physical recursive self-improvement, where experience improves the ability to learn subsequent tasks.

repos.title: Apodex 1.1: Scaling Agentic Intelligence for Complex Work
repos.paper_summary: Apodex 1.1 is a model and execution system that scales agentic intelligence for long-horizon tasks by expanding executable environments and coordinating parallel agents. It defines "working capability" as sustained, verifiable progress through stateful interactions with files, search, and code. The method uses Environment Scaling to generate diverse task worlds with explicit verifiers, and Agentic Coordination Scaling to train decomposition, delegation, and replanning behaviors. A shared runtime, AgentOS, maintains persistent workspace state and provenance across tools and agents. Training combines supervised fine-tuning with PIVOT-RL, which localizes reinforcement learning at critical decision points identified via hindsight analysis. On professional work benchmarks, Apodex 1.1 with Agent Team scores 38.5 on APEX-Agents and 78.8% win rate on GDPVal, matching or exceeding leading systems like GPT-5.6-Sol and Claude-Opus-4.8. In finance simulations, it achieves a net worth of USD 1,038,255 on YC-Bench using ReAct, and 54.3 on FrontierFinance with Agent Team. A 35B-parameter mini version retains strong performance in a locally deployable form. Limitations include the run-scoped nature of coordination state, which lacks atomic checkpointing with the filesystem, and the reliance on internal harness reproductions for some external benchmark comparisons.

repos.title: $τ^2$-Bench: Evaluating Conversational Agents in a Dual-Control Environment
repos.paper_summary: τ2-bench introduces a dual-control benchmark for conversational agents, modeled as a Dec-POMDP where both the agent and a simulated user possess tools to modify a shared environment. The paper releases a telecom domain with 114 tasks generated programmatically from atomic subtasks, alongside a compositional task generator that ensures verifiable correctness. By constraining user simulator behavior through specific tool affordances rather than natural language prompts alone, the method reduces user simulation errors to 16% (6% critical), compared to 40% (12% critical) in previous retail domains. Experiments show significant performance degradation when shifting from autonomous operation to dual-control; `gpt-4.1` pass^1 drops by 18%, and `o4-mini` drops by 25%. In the default dual-control setting, `gpt-4.1` achieves a 34% pass^1 rate on new telecom tasks, while `claude-3.7-sonnet` reaches 49%. The benchmark does not explicitly model the expert-novice gap, and extending domain coverage currently relies on human curation.

repos.title: Has GPT-6-Astra Achieved Embodied Intelligence?
repos.paper_summary: This technical report evaluates GPT-6-Astra, a model whose weights stay fixed, on 12 embodied benchmarks covering tabletop manipulation, dexterous hands, humanoids, household tasks, and navigation. Under a unified protocol, the model gets a frozen knowledge package built from each benchmark's training demonstrations, and episodes run with either the standard step limit or up to 10× that limit. At the standard budget, it matches or exceeds the best published result on most settings, with the largest margins on LIBERO-Ultra-Long and DexJoCo. Reported success rates are 81.9% on RoboDojo and 87.3% on DexJoCo. On SIMPLE, task-level ICL raises success on four common tasks from 70.8% to 90.8%. In a RoboDojo harness ablation pairing the model with a π0.5 controller, closed-loop review plus ICL reaches 54.17% success, versus 15.56% for the baseline. Limitations include weaker transfer when test tasks differ from the training data, high token and time cost, and failures in physical verification, irreversible errors, and long-horizon progress.

digest_headlines.heading: Introduction
digest_headlines.headline: The report asks what a general model's embodied competence implies, and where the field should go next.

digest_headlines.heading: Large-Scale Study under A Unified Protocol
digest_headlines.headline: At the standard budget, the model matches or exceeds the best published result on most of twelve settings.

digest_headlines.heading: Harness Ablation
digest_headlines.headline: Closed-loop review improves success by up to 20.00 percentage points over open-loop execution, at higher token cost.

digest_headlines.heading: Real-World Validation
digest_headlines.headline: Zero-shot control succeeded in 17/18 rigid pick-and-place trials but 0/11 plug insertion trials.

digest_headlines.heading: Towards a Next-Generation Embodied Benchmark
digest_headlines.headline: Current benchmarks were designed for imitation-trained policies, so the report proposes three principles for next-generation designs.

digest_headlines.heading: Conclusion
digest_headlines.headline: GPT-6-Astra is a clear advance in embodied capability, but benchmark success does not yet imply reliable deployment.

digest_headlines.heading: Appendix
digest_headlines.headline: The appendix lists contributors, related work, empirical studies of frontier models, and per-platform real-world results.

repos.title: Fewer Tokens, Better Action: GPT-6 Astra Robot Agents with 14% Higher Success Rate but 65% Fewer Tokens
repos.paper_summary:
PyRUA-Lean is an interactive code-execution framework for vision-language model (VLM) robot agents that reduces token overhead while improving task success. The agent generates Python cells that compose classical robot primitives and learned vision-language-action policies, executing conditional checks and local retries within the runtime. Only explicitly requested images and state feedback are returned to the VLM for replanning, whereas intermediate results remain in a persistent program state.

Across 700 simulated task instances from LIBERO-PRO, RoboTwin 2.0, and RoboCasa365, PyRUA-Lean increases overall success from 63.1% to 71.7% compared to a tool-calling baseline using the same GPT-6 Astra planner. On instances solved by both agents, it uses 49% fewer LLM calls and 65% fewer input tokens, reducing estimated cost per episode from USD 1.63 to USD 0.74. Ablations show these gains persist without VLA policies or operating guides. Limitations include evaluation restricted to simulation with one run per instance, and efficiency gains diminish on tasks dominated by VLA policies where initial prompts account for much of the input cost.
